description: Springy, chewy alkaline noodles from plain flour — baking soda baked into a stronger alkali, the Momofuku way.
equipment_html: Glass jar with a lid (for the baked soda)
Pasta machine with a thin (linguine-style) cutter

hero.alt: Ramen noodles with baked baking soda

ingredients.name: Baked baking soda (make ahead, keeps for months)

intro_html: Ramen noodles get their bounce and yellow tint from an alkaline salt (kansui). The Momofuku trick: bake ordinary baking soda for an hour and it turns into a much stronger alkali (sodium carbonate). Dissolve it in the water, make a stiff dough, rest it, and roll it through a pasta machine. Use these for the ramen or the ginger scallion noodles.

notes.html:
• Heat drives off water and carbon dioxide and leaves sodium carbonate — the main salt in kansui.
  • More alkalinity makes the flour hold more water and gives the springy, chewy bite that stays firm in hot broth, plus the faint yellow colour and that typical ramen smell.

• These are starting points from the Momofuku / Lucky Peach recipe (400 g flour, 12 g baked soda, 200 ml water).
  • The dough is stiff on purpose; if it really won’t come together after the first rest, add water a teaspoon at a time.
  • The magazine version used all-purpose flour only — the bread flour here adds chew.

• Adapted from the Momofuku (David Chang) / Lucky Peach method (Lucky Peach issue 1, 2011), using Harold McGee’s baked baking soda.
  • Written in my own words.

sources.label: Brains for brunch — homemade ramen (Lucky Peach noodles)
Biting at the Bits — baked baking soda

steps.body_html:
• Line a tray with foil and spread the baking soda out in a thin, even layer.
  • Bake at 120 °C (250 °F) for 1 hour. It loses about a third of its weight as it turns into sodium carbonate.
  • Let it cool, tip it into a glass jar, close it and label it. It’s a much stronger alkali than baking soda now — handle it with gloves, keep it away from eyes and don’t taste it.

how.caption: Spread the baking soda thinly on a foil-lined tray, then bake 1 hour at 120 °C.

steps.title: Bake the baking soda

steps.body_html:
• Wearing gloves, stir until fully dissolved:
    • baked baking soda 12 g (4 tsp)
    • warm water 100 ml
  • Then add:
    • cold water 100 ml

how.caption: Gloves on: stir the baked soda into the warm water until it fully dissolves.

steps.title: Make the alkaline water

steps.body_html:
• Put in a large bowl:
    • bread flour 200 g
    • all-purpose flour 200 g
  • Pour in the alkaline water while stirring with chopsticks, then work it together with your hands.
  • It will look too dry and crumbly — that’s right; it comes together while kneading and resting.

how.caption: Pour in the alkaline water while stirring with chopsticks, then work it with your hands.

steps.title: Mix the dough

steps.body_html:
• Knead for 5 minutes, pressing hard with the heel of your hand — the dough is stiff.
  • Wrap it and rest 20 minutes.
  • Knead another 5 minutes until smooth, wrap again and rest 1 hour (fridge is fine).

how.caption: Knead hard with the heel of your hand for 5 minutes — it's a stiff dough.

steps.title: Knead, rest, knead

steps.body_html:
• Cut the dough into 4 pieces and flatten each one with your palm.
  • Run each through the pasta machine on the widest setting, fold in half and run it again — 3–4 times until it’s smooth.
  • Then step down to the third-thickest setting (about 1.5 mm), dusting with starch so it doesn’t stick.

how.caption: Run each piece through the widest setting, fold it, and repeat 3–4 times.
Then step down to the third-thickest setting, dusting with starch.

steps.title: Sheet it

steps.body_html:
• Run the sheets through the thin cutter, pulling the noodles out from underneath rather than pushing them.
  • Toss with a little starch and shape into loose nests of about 130 g.
  • Cook now, keep in a bag in the fridge 2–3 days, or freeze the nests and cook them from frozen.

how.caption: Run the sheets through the thin cutter, pulling the noodles out from underneath.
Toss with starch and shape into loose nests of about 130 g.

steps.title: Cut and portion

steps.body_html:
• Boil in plenty of unsalted water for 1½–2 minutes — taste one: springy and cooked through.
  • Lift out with a strainer, shake off the water well, and straight into the bowl.

how.caption: Boil 1½–2 minutes, then lift out and shake off the water well.

steps.title: Cook

timeline.note_html: The baked soda keeps for months in its jar — after the first batch, skip the first bar.
